TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN

What goes into a rank?

Stars follow the repository. We sum stars on public, non-fork repositories owned by each personal GitHub account, with a GitHub-detected SPDX license other than NONE or NOASSERTION. Archived repositories count and are labeled.

Organization-owned projects aren’t credited to individuals here. Ownership doesn’t prove original authorship or sole maintenance. Stars measure attention, and can be manipulated; they aren’t a measure of developer skill or unique users.

This is a snapshot of a curated sample, not a complete global ranking. Browse every eligible repository in the Projects tab or open a developer’s full profile. Date ranges filter each repository’s latest push as of the dataset date (UTC). Last week is the previous Monday–Sunday; last month is the previous calendar month. Today and rolling periods include the dataset date. These are activity filters, not historical star-growth rankings. Interest filters use keyword matching in repository names, descriptions, and available GitHub topics; categories can overlap and are not verified classifications. Search, interest, minimum-star, and language filters limit the repositories used for developer totals. The archive filter excludes archived repositories from both views. Recently pushed sorts by GitHub’s last push timestamp; it does not measure commits, releases, or maintenance quality. No growth rates are shown until historical snapshots exist.

Source: GitHub public repository API ↗
